bull_bear.body: Dividend: INR 1/share (50p regular + 50p special); Buyback announced previously; ESOPs: 8.3 lakh shares granted over 9 years; Promoter action: Gifted shares to charitable trust to avoid capital gains tax; Potential promoter dilution/pledge up to 3% by Oct 2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Receivables concentration (INR 108cr AR, 90-day terms from Fortune 500); Client concentration (Top 5 = 40%); No formal revenue guidance; Currency volatility (no active hedging policy since Jan 2026); Execution risk on 100% AI-adoption target.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and transparent; Emphasizes 'breakout year' after 2-year plateau; Pragmatic on margins (willing to normalize to 24%); Innovative focus on proprietary AI tools ('Insane SDD', 'RAI'); Candid on hedging failures and receivables logic.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Promoters gifted shares to a trust specifically to avoid personal capital gains tax burden, signaling tax-efficient wealth transfer rather than market exit; The 'campus' is effectively a real estate arbitrage (free land from MP govt) creating a hidden asset on balance sheet with 60% leasable surplus; 'Insane SDD' attempts to productize service delivery, potentially decoupling revenue from linear headcount growth.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Two buybacks completed, "in 2021 and 2025", with the second buyback accompanied by a 3:1 bonus.
- Two acquisitions completed and cited as successful: US-based Philosophie Group, Inc. and Pune-based Eternus.
- Balance sheet carries cash and cash equivalent of Rs.360 Cr for 2025-26, which the deck notes "includes AR of 119 Cr".
- The deck makes no dividend statement and gives no stated capital-allocation policy beyond the buyback, bonus and acquisition history.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Durable client franchise — 95% of clients give repeat business and the company reports over 90% of business coming from existing customers
- AI-led delivery at scale — 43% of FY26 revenue generated through AI-augmented software development, with proprietary AI-native solutions (InsaneSDD 2.0, InfoBeans RAI, Expona 2.0)
- Process maturity moat — CMMI Level 5 appraisal, the highest level of a globally recognised process framework
- Deep platform-ecosystem positions — 11 years in the ServiceNow ecosystem with a 4.9/5 CSAT and the ServiceNow Transformation Partner Award APAC; a Salesforce practice with 400+ consultants-scale credentials, 2,000+ project implementations, 800+ certifications and 80+ AppExchange products implemented (as stated in the report)
- Long-term technology partnerships with Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft, Azure, UiPath and agineo, including a 2024 strategic partnership with agineo GmbH, Germany's elite ServiceNow partner
- Inorganic capability build-out through the acquisitions of Philosophie Group, Inc. and Eternus Solutions Pvt. Ltd.
- Employer brand and ownership culture — Great Place to Work for the 10th consecutive year, 175 team members across 2 ESOP schemes over 9 years and 8,30,060 stock options granted till now
- Diversified geographic delivery and revenue footprint across the US, Europe, UAE and APAC
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration of revenue in the US geography — The US remains the largest market and continues to face a relatively uncertain macro environment; management says this is mitigated by the growing European and Middle East contribution, but the exposure remains a structural sensitivity to US client spending.
- Project-based revenue with limited multi-year order visibility — Management explicitly flags that the project-based revenue model constrains forward predictability — there is no multi-year order book underpinning revenue.
- Pace of AI-led change demanding continuous reinvestment — Staying ahead requires continuous reinvestment in skills, accelerators and governance; falling behind the AI transition would erode the company's core differentiation, which is an AI-first operating model.
- Competition for skilled AI and technology talent, and a shifting hiring pyramid — Intensifying competition for AI-capable talent affects both delivery capacity and cost structure in a business where employee costs are the dominant input.
- Cyber security and data-protection exposure — Heightened cyber security and data-protection risks are flagged as a threat, and Data Privacy and Security is identified in the BRSR as a material risk driven by rising cyberthreats and more stringent data protection laws; mitigation is through regular security audits, encryption, staff training and data-protection protocols.
- Margin pressure from escalating operating and talent costs — Management flags margin pressure during periods of high investment, consistent with its position that FY26 profitability sat above steady-state levels and should not be treated as a new baseline.
- Global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty — Uncertainty is flagged as affecting client spending trajectories, with the Company's risk framework overseen by the Risk Management Committee which frames, implements and monitors the risk management plan and reviews its effectiveness.
- Rapid technology evolution requiring continuous upskilling — The pace of technology evolution necessitates continuous upskilling of the workforce; the Company reports 44,970 man-hours of learning during FY26 and collaboration with the IIMs as its mitigation.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Evolve into an AI-native data and engineering company — positioning to lead, not follow, the transition to AI-augmented software delivery, with one founder now dedicated full-time to driving the AI and products agenda.
- Build and scale a proprietary AI accelerator portfolio spanning specification-driven development, enterprise knowledge retrieval and AI-led quality assurance (InsaneSDD 2.0, InfoBeans RAI, Expona 2.0, BeanTrail, Stanza).
- Deepen existing client relationships and grow wallet share of client tech spends, supplemented by selective addition of new enterprise clients.
- Continue geographic diversification — the US remains the largest market while Europe (led by Germany, supported by the agineo partnership) and the Middle East scale up; diversification is stated as a continuing strategic priority.
- Invest meaningfully and continuously in AI capabilities, sales and go-to-market, market expansion and people.
- Evaluate selective acquisition opportunities where they fit the company's strategy and culture.
- Anchor AI delivery in responsible-AI governance — early adoption of ISO/IEC 42001:2023, the first international standard for AI Management Systems, formalising governance, risk-management and lifecycle frameworks for AI deployments.
- Deepen platform-ecosystem alliances (ServiceNow, Salesforce, Microsoft, agineo) as a differentiation and demand channel.
- Maintain a conservative and consistent capital-allocation philosophy: a strong net-debt-free balance sheet, invest first in growth, capability-building and selective acquisitions, and return surplus to shareholders in a steady, predictable manner.
- The Company's governance disclosures frame capital allocation through shareholder-return decisions taken at Board and AGM level rather than a formal quantified policy in this section. For the year ended 31st March 2026 the Board, at its meeting held on April 28, 2026, recommended a final dividend of INR 0.50 (Fifty Paise) per equity share along with a special dividend of INR 0.50 (Fifty Paise) per equity share, put to members as an ordinary-business item at the 16th AGM to be held on 07th August 2026; the record date for both the final and special dividend is 31st July 2026, with payment after AGM approval made electronically to members whose bank details are updated and by dividend warrant/banker's cheque/demand draft otherwise. Governance philosophy is stated as maximising shareholder value legally, ethically and on a sustainable basis while ensuring fairness to every shareholder and preserving the interests of multiple stakeholders, with good governance treated as a key driver of sustainable corporate growth and long-term stakeholder value creation.
- Goal to attain carbon neutrality / net-zero carbon emissions in the Company's operations by 2030, pursued through energy-efficient technology, renewable energy sources and carbon offset programmes (BRSR specific commitment and director's ESG statement).
- BRSR Core disclosures assessed/assured externally — Type-2 (High Level) assurance as per AA1000ASv3 by Ecopurus Sustainability Solutions Private Limited, signed 13th July 2026.
- ESG Committee of the Board is the highest authority responsible for implementation and oversight of the business responsibility policies and is the decision-making body on sustainability-related issues; it is also the reviewing authority for the environmental principle (P6).
- Standards adopted and mapped to the NGRBC principles: ISO 14001:2015 (environmental management) and ISO 45001:2018 (occupational health & safety), and ISO 27001 (information security).
- All nine NGRBC principles are covered by board-approved policies that have been translated into procedures; policy extension to value-chain partners currently applies to Principle 9 only.
- Establish volunteering and community involvement programmes covering team members, and continue education of underprivileged students through InfoBeans Foundation and support to other educational institutes.
- Diversity representation disclosed at 33.33% female participation on both the Board of Directors and among Key Management Personnel; women are 28.3% of total employees.
- Material responsible-business issues identified are Data Privacy and Security (risk), Talent Management (opportunity) and Climate Change Events (opportunity), each with a stated mitigation/adaptation approach and positive financial implications.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for all stakeholder groups — communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners — with publicly published CSR and Whistle-Blower policies.
- Internal control and governance framework strengthened during the year with fraud risk assessment processes, mandatory leave policies, strengthened employee background verification, an improved whistle-blower framework and a more robust enterprise risk management structure.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: As an IT services company, InfoBeans discloses no plant, capacity or physical capex programme in the annual report; expansion is described as capability-, talent- and geography-led. The stated playbook is to build capacity for growth by expanding talent aligned to business demand, strengthening leadership and capability-development initiatives, enhancing delivery readiness across service lines and investing in future-ready skills and emerging technologies, while continuing to invest in AI-native capabilities and proprietary frameworks and accelerators across the organisation. Footprint expansion is targeted at the US, Germany and the Middle East, with deeper regional client and partner relationships, focused client acquisition and stronger local market engagement and business development; ecosystem expansion runs through the Salesforce and ServiceNow platforms and partner networks. Inorganic expansion is a formal pillar — the Company continues to evaluate acquisitions aligned with its long-term strategy to add domain expertise and specialised capabilities, access new clients, markets and talent pools, and create value through disciplined integration. The physical estate referenced is historical rather than forward: workspaces at Crystal IT Park Indore (the 'World of WOW'), a Pune office and later a Pune SEZ office, and a 35,000 sq. ft. state-of-the-art facility added in Indore, alongside acquisitions of Philosophie Group, Inc. and Eternus Solutions Pvt. Ltd. On the environmental side, the Company commits to accelerating investment in sustainable and innovative technologies and to SBTi-validated emission reduction pathways to FY2033.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Enterprises increasingly expect AI-augmented delivery with higher productivity, faster cycles and better quality outcomes than the traditional model allowed — management calls this one of the most important transitions the industry has experienced in decades.
- Growth in FY26 was broad-based and predominantly organic, well-distributed across geographies and service lines, with a meaningful portion of incremental revenue from expansion within existing client relationships plus 24 new clients added during the year.
- Client-franchise depth as a demand driver: 50 large enterprise clients of which 18 are Fortune 500, approximately 90%+ of revenue each year from repeat business, and average client relationship tenure now exceeding 9 years.
- Margin levers cited: improved resource utilisation and allocation, a focused service mix, a controlled cost structure and prudent hiring aligned to demand.
- Management frames FY26 profitability as above steady-state and sustainable levels (~24% EBITDA, ~14% PAT) and the result of a strong operating year rather than a new baseline.
- Geographic diversification proved valuable in a year marked by macro-economic uncertainty in the United States.
- Worldwide IT spending is expected to reach USD 6.31 trillion in 2026, a 13.5% increase over 2025, driven by AI infrastructure and software, producing an increasingly multi-speed market in which AI-centric segments significantly outperform traditional categories.
- IT services remains the single largest global segment at USD 1,870 billion, growing 9.0% in 2026; software spending is projected to grow 15.1% with generative AI driving outsized gains.
- The Indian technology industry crossed the USD 300 billion revenue milestone for the first time in FY26 (estimated USD 315 billion, up 6.1%), with exports exceeding USD 246 billion (+5.6%) and growth in APAC and the Middle East outpacing mature geographies.
- Industry hiring has shifted from volume-led recruitment to a skill-mix approach prioritising AI fluency, problem solving and domain expertise, with more than two million professionals upskilled in AI during the year.
- Macro backdrop: global growth projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 (below the recent 3.4% pace), with downside risks dominating — energy-price shocks, geopolitical fragmentation, renewed trade tensions and a possible reassessment of AI-driven productivity expectations.
- India remained among the fastest-growing major economies with real GDP estimated to grow 7.4% in FY26, services-led growth continuing to support demand for the country's technology and engineering capabilities.
- No formal order book is disclosed; revenue visibility is described through repeat business — approximately 90%+ of revenue each year comes from repeat clients, with average relationship tenure exceeding 9 years and 24 new clients added during FY26.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: InfoBeans broke the INR 400cr revenue plateau with 32% FY26 growth, driven by a strategic pivot to AI-augmented delivery (43% of revenue) targeting 100% penetration within 12 months. Margin expansion (PAT up 104% YoY) demonstrates operating leverage, though receivables bloated due to Fortune 500 payment cycles. The shift from pure services to owning a strategic campus (60% leasable) adds an asset-light real estate optionality while securing long-term cost stability.

meta.thesis: InfoBeans broke the INR 400cr revenue plateau with 32% FY26 growth, driven by a strategic pivot to AI-augmented delivery (43% of revenue) targeting 100% penetration within 12 months. Margin expansion (PAT up 104% YoY) demonstrates operating leverage, though receivables bloated due to Fortune 500 payment cycles. The shift from pure services to owning a strategic campus (60% leasable) adds an asset-light real estate optionality while securing long-term cost stability.
